findings.problem: TC-RPT-061 is defined twice with two unrelated bodies: current-backend-test-plan.md line 875 defines it as 'Hand-over with an undeclared field cannot reach the store' (traces AC-RPT-061, REQ-RPT-053 — the ADR-RPT-018 fix added at this revise; backend header now reads 'TCs : 61 (TC-RPT-001 … TC-RPT-061)'), while current-frontend-test-plan.md line 17 independently defines TC-RPT-061 as 'CheckReport model, RUNNING Check' (traces AC-RPT-027, REQ-RPT-023) and continues its own range through TC-RPT-070 — its header literally states 'TCs : 10 (TC-RPT-061 … TC-RPT-070)'. Sibling modules get this right (CHK's backend ends at TC-CHK-100, frontend starts at TC-CHK-101; DOC's backend ends at TC-DOC-077, frontend starts at TC-DOC-078): the frontend plan continues the backend's TC-{MOD}-* sequence with no overlap. RPT's frontend plan was never re-bumped when this revise's backend fix inserted a new TC-RPT-061, so the two plans now collide on one id with two different acceptance meanings. The collision is severe enough that traceability.md (line 285) silently resolves it by attributing TC-RPT-061 only to backend-test-plan — the frontend's TC-RPT-061 definition is entirely absent from the 'Defined in' column of the generated matrix, i.e. invisible to every C10 registry-agree check and to gov.py split. gov.py analyze's own C10.10/C10.11 (71/10 subjects examined) did not catch it, so this is a genuine adversarial-review catch, not a re-flagged machine finding.
findings.fix: Renumber every case of current-frontend-test-plan.md from TC-RPT-061…070 to TC-RPT-062…071 (shift +1, continuing from the backend plan's true last id, 61): the file header ('TCs : 10 (TC-RPT-062 … TC-RPT-071)'), every `<!-- TC:TC-RPT-0XX:START/END -->` marker and `### TC-RPT-0XX` heading, the PHASE/SUB `traces=` lists, and the TC TRACEABILITY INDEX table — then regenerate traceability.md so AC-RPT-027's 'Referenced by' column and TC-RPT-062's 'Defined in' row agree.

findings.problem: REQ-RPT-009 ('if any part of a completed report cannot be stored, then the system shall store no part of it, keep the Check RUNNING and refuse the call as not stored') covers two distinct unwanted paths: a validation refusal (an out-of-list code, etc.) and a genuine technical/persistence failure during the INSERT step — the backend-execution-plan's completeCheck step 4 and its in-process rejection-codes table both name this second path explicitly as RPT-500-REPORT-NOT-STORED / ReportNotStoredException with the caller's whole transaction rolled back. But AC-RPT-012 — REQ-RPT-009's only AC — and its sole TC (TC-RPT-012) exercise only the first path (an out-of-list finding outcome `PASSED`, RULE-RPT-006 → RPT-422-UNKNOWN-CODE). No TC anywhere asserts the 500 code, the whole-rollback, or that the Check stays RUNNING after an actual write failure. This is a real gap, not a convention exclusion: fault-injection TCs for exactly this class of path already exist elsewhere in the same plan (TC-RPT-060, for the purge's per-row DELETE failure) — RPT's own completeCheck persistence failure is the one such path left untested.
findings.fix: Add a TC (a second AC under REQ-RPT-009, or broaden AC-RPT-012's Given/When/Then into two) that fault-injects a failure during the Finding/Check Document/Unread Query INSERT step of completeCheck and asserts: ReportNotStoredException / RPT-500-REPORT-NOT-STORED is raised; 0 rows are left in RPT_FINDING/RPT_CHECK_DOCUMENT/RPT_UNREAD_QUERY for that Check; OVERALL_STATUS stays null; the Check stays RUNNING.

findings.problem: RULE-RPT-003 explicitly names AWAITING_DOCUMENTS → FAILED as an allowed transition (alongside RUNNING → FAILED), and the db-script's CHK_RPT_CHECK_RUN_RESULT / CHK_RPT_CHECK_RUN_AWAITING CHECK constraints correctly permit it. This is a real scenario — a manual-fetch Check whose upload window expires before it ever starts running (failureReason UPLOAD_WINDOW_EXPIRED, a code already in the closed list). Yet every failCheck TC in the backend test plan (TC-RPT-010, TC-RPT-021, TC-RPT-059) preconditions the Check as RUNNING; none preconditions AWAITING_DOCUMENTS (confirmed: 'AWAITING_DOCUMENTS' appears in the plan only for createCheckRun, markRunning and completeCheck-refusal cases, never for a failCheck case). The one transition RULE-RPT-003 names twice is tested from only one of its two starting states.
findings.fix: Add a TC deriving from REQ-RPT-018 (or a new AC) with precondition 'Check N is AWAITING_DOCUMENTS', exercising failCheck(N, UPLOAD_WINDOW_EXPIRED, detail, endedAt), asserting the Check ends FAILED with that reason, overallStatus null, 0 findings — mirroring TC-RPT-021 but from the AWAITING_DOCUMENTS start state.

findings.clause: P1 unwanted-pattern / observability (feature-unwanted, C5.16 adjacent); adr:true
findings.problem: REQ-RPT-052 ('If the deletion of any record of an expired Check run fails during the purge, then the system shall keep that Check run with all its records and continue') and its AC/TC (AC-RPT-060, TC-RPT-060) correctly specify the keep-and-continue behaviour, and REQ-RPT-046 requires logging only the count deleted and the cut-off. Neither requirement, nor TC-RPT-060's Expected line, asks for the id of the Check run whose deletion failed (or the cause) to be logged. A Check run that fails every purge run indefinitely (e.g. a stuck FK or lock) is therefore invisible in the logs beyond a deleted-count that silently stays one short each night — a counter-case of the raw-idea §12 guardrail 'nothing skipped silently' (already cited for REQ-RPT-011/012/014) not extended to the purge's own skip path.
findings.fix: Extend REQ-RPT-052 (or add a sibling REQ) to state: 'When a Check run's deletion fails during the purge, the system shall log its Check run identifier and the failure cause before continuing with the next expired Check run,' with a matching AC/TC addition to TC-RPT-060's Expected line. Best-practice choice (extend REQ-RPT-052 vs. a new unwanted-pattern REQ) needs confirming.
